dispositions.reason: No Linux release, kernel interface or file-system baseline is named, by the owner's decision of 2026-11-25, as for cabinet-kernel (its A20 rule 3 and decision 34, 2026-10-18, where State 2 round 134 asked the same): a host on which opening without following a link, binding exclusively, renaming or flushing does not act as Linux documents it is unsupported, so A17's exclusive-listener guarantee is stated for the host it was written for and claims nothing on another.

dispositions.topic_text: Exact CPython 3.12 patch release and pinned artifact digest
dispositions.what: Which exact CPython 3.12 patch a release pins (rule 1 already requires an exact version and digest; rule 6 fixes the family and minor line). Options: pin the current approved 3.12 patch per release; keep one patch across releases until a verified dependency-update release; take the patch the selected base image fixes. Every option must keep: an exact CPython 3.12.x named with its digest in the release's list, verified by A20 Required tests 1, 2 and 5.
keeps:
1. A release names every dependency it runs with, at an exact version, with
   its digest: every Python package, direct or transitive, by the digest of
   its distribution file; the Python version; and the base image of VM
   Platform's Registry environment by its digest, which fixes the system
   libraries and the store's engine.
options: Pin the current approved CPython 3.12 patch for each release.
Keep one exact CPython 3.12 patch across releases until a verified dependency-update release changes it.
Use the exact CPython 3.12 patch fixed by the selected base image.
consequences: Changing the patch changes a runtime dependency and requires a new verified release.
Holding a patch improves reproducibility but can defer runtime fixes.
Letting the base image determine it couples interpreter updates to base-image selection.
